comment: Mutation testing for the ROUND-27 MEMBER-RESOLUTION PHASES. A fifth config targeting the SAME project as stryker-config.json but a disjoint set of files, because the two measure different things and must not share a floor: the original generator leg guards four small deliberately-chosen files (EquatableArray, BlittableProof, ConstructorSelector, LocationInfo) and has held break 84 for several rounds, and folding new lines into it would collapse that number in a way indistinguishable from a regression in the four it protects. WHY THIS LEG EXISTS: round 27 extracted 13 new Pipeline/ files from three giant methods, and the brief asked for the moved functions to be covered 'close to 100 % from mutation and other standpoints'. Line coverage (94.5 %) and reach (32/32 methods) were delivered; MUTATION coverage of those functions was 0 %, because no leg's mutate globs named any of the new files. WHY ONLY THREE FILES. The first attempt scoped this leg at all 13 extracted files (6,659 lines). Measured 2026-08-27: Stryker generated 13,129 mutants, discarded 3,240 as compile errors and filtered 8,049 as out-of-leg, leaving 1,353 to test -- and after 158 minutes on 12 cores it had not finished, while leaking idle vstest testhost processes (26 of 32 alive with no CPU). That is not a gate anyone can run: it exceeds the nightly CI budget by an order of magnitude, and it did not reliably terminate locally either. The run was abandoned deliberately rather than left to finish, and the cost curve it produced is the evidence for the scoping here. So this leg takes ONE AREA, the way Issues/round27/AUDIT-mutation-scope.md already recommended: the four member-resolution phases (ApplySkipNullSourceMembers, ResolveMapValues, ResolveExplicitMaps, ResolveAutoMatchedMembers) plus the two context records they are parameterised by. MEASURED 2026-08-27 on 12 cores: 236 tested mutants of 13,129 created (9,583 filtered as out-of-leg, 3,240 rolled back as compile errors), 37 minutes wall-clock, 184 detected of 239 scoreable = 76.99 %. The estimate beforehand was ~190 from the abandoned run's density of ~0.20 tested mutants per line; the real figure is 236, and the estimate is recorded here only so the density heuristic can be judged against it when the next area is sized. The other ten extracted files stay uncovered and are named in the audit as the follow-on programme, one area per leg, each with its own measured floor. NOTE -- the mutate globs are PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.Generator, so a repo-root path matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard. NOTE -- files are listed explicitly rather than globbed with 'Pipeline/*.cs', so adding one is a deliberate act that shows up in review AND cannot silently push the leg back over its CI budget; the four sibling configs follow the same convention. NOTE -- break/low are pinned to the FIRST MEASURED score, floored, exactly as the CodeFixes leg was (52.54 -> break 52, later raised to 87 by killing survivors). Raise break only by killing survivors, never by re-measuring on a lucky run; the floor moves in the same commit as the kills that earned it.
